title: fix(plugin-auth): mount the OIDC discovery routes before the socket opens, not after the auth instance builds
body:
Fixes #21078
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`plugin-auth` mounts its OIDC discovery routes during the same synchronous call that registers its other routes. That call runs from the `kernel:ready` route hook, which comes before `kernel:listening` opens the socket. Each handler then gets the better-auth instance on each request.

- **Before.** `registerAuthRoutes` started `registerOidcDiscoveryRoutes(...)` with `void` and did not wait for it. That method awaited `getAuthInstance()` before it called `rawApp.get(...)`, so the routes were added whenever the instance finished building. Sometimes that was after the server had already matched a first request. Hono freezes its matcher on the first match. The late `get` then threw `Can not add a route since the matcher is already built`, the error was caught and logged, and both doors answered 404 until the process restarted.
- **After.** `registerOidcDiscoveryRoutes` is synchronous and every `rawApp.get` runs before it returns. If a route cannot be mounted, the error leaves the hook and fails the boot through the kernel's propagating `kernel:ready` dispatch. It is not caught.

### Config-level vs instance-level (zone 2, item 2)

| Fact | Known | Where it is decided now |
|---|---|---|
| Discovery on at all (`resolveOidcProviderEnabled`) | config | at mount (unchanged) |
| Issuer, plain-HTTP posture, both transport notices | config (`getAuthIssuer()`) | at mount |
| RFC 8414 path-inserted alias (base path) | config | at mount |
| RFC 9728 documents: env switch and `isMcpOAuthEnabled()` | config | at mount |
| oauthProvider plugin degraded (`getDegradedAuthFeatures`) | instance | per request: `next()`, the answer the path gave when it was not mounted |
| The instance the vendor document builders read | instance | per request, through `getAuthInstance()` (single-flight and memoised in `AuthManager`) |

All of the mount decisions can be made from config, so the change needed no late `get` and there was no fork to report.

### Kept on purpose: one boot-time preparation call, which mounts nothing

After the routes are mounted, the method calls the same instance-level resolution once and does not wait for it. The old await-then-mount code did three things at boot, and this call keeps them:
1. The better-auth instance is still built in the background at boot. It is not moved to the first request that needs it. That would put the vendor plugins' `init` writes inside the serving window, which is a separate change.
2. A degraded oauthProvider is still reported once at boot, at ERROR, naming the cause.
3. If the documents cannot be built from the instance, the failure is still reported at boot, at ERROR, under the same opening words: `Failed to register OIDC discovery routes`. `scripts/publish-smoke.sh` (SMOKE_BOOT_ERROR_PATTERN) matches that text by name in its boot window, so a pin holds those words as a grep anchor.

Both outcomes are logged, and a request that hits the same failure gets the server's error response (500). The next request tries the build again. The old code answered 404 for the life of the process.

## Census: late route registration in `plugin-auth` (zone 2, item 3)

| Site | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `/.well-known/openid-configuration` | **fixed** | was `rawApp.get` after `await getAuthInstance()`; now synchronous |
| `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` | **fixed** | same |
| `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` plus the auth base path (RFC 8414 §3.1 alias) | **fixed** | same method, same shape |
| `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (RFC 9728) | **fixed** | same method, mounted after the await whenever the MCP OAuth track was live |
| `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` plus the MCP path | **fixed** | same |
| Every other route in `registerAuthRoutes` (IP-gate `use`, `config` / `bootstrap-status` GETs, the admin / SSO / organization / OAuth-application / verification POSTs, the `all` catch-all) | already compliant | `registerAuthRoutes` returns `void` and is synchronous. Every `await` in its body is inside a handler, never before a `rawApp.*` call. |
| Other `void` dispatches in `auth-plugin.ts` (settings re-apply callbacks for branding, localization and auth settings) | out of scope: they register no route | they only re-read settings |
| Other files in `plugin-auth/src` | none mount routes | `getRawApp`, `'http-server'` and `IHttpServer` appear only in `auth-plugin.ts` |

## Pins and ablations

New file `src/oidc-discovery-sync-mount.test.ts` runs the real `registerAuthRoutes` on a real Hono app, with the real `@better-auth/oauth-provider` document builders over a fake `auth.api`. Only `AuthManager` is a stand-in, so the test controls when the instance resolves.

| Test | HEAD | Ablation A: forbidden shape put back (mount after `await`, `void`, caught and logged) | Ablation B: the pre-fix `auth-plugin.ts` itself (BASE `53ed3d10`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| control: late but IDLE (instance resolves, then the first request) | pass | **pass** | **pass** |
| a request that lands before the instance resolves does not freeze the doors out | pass | FAIL: `[openid-configuration, 404]` | FAIL: 404 |
| a discovery request that arrives first waits, then 200 | pass | FAIL: `[404, 404]` | FAIL |
| alias and RFC 9728 documents survive the early request | pass | FAIL | FAIL |
| every discovery path is on the router when `registerAuthRoutes` returns | pass | FAIL: 5 paths missing | FAIL |
| a route that cannot mount fails the hook (not caught and logged) | pass | FAIL: nothing thrown | FAIL |
| degraded oauthProvider: doors answer byte-identical to the unmounted composition, reported once naming the cause | pass | pass | FAIL on the report only. The doors matched the unmounted composition on BASE too, so the wire answer is unchanged. |
| instance cannot be built: smoke anchor logged once, 500, then 200 after recovery | pass | FAIL: 404 | FAIL |

Ablation A went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: anchor 1 to 0, marker 0 to 1, blob `c11a3fa6` to `83ec14c2`, restored to blob == HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty. Ablation B wrote BASE's blob `f2324f20` over the file under an `EXIT INT TERM` trap and restored to blob `c11a3fa6` == HEAD with `git diff HEAD` empty. The subject is imported from `src` by relative path, so neither leg needs a rebuild.

Three route-only fixtures (`auth-catchall-fallthrough`, `auth-catchall-yield`, `admin-sso-bridge-gate`) now compose the plugin with `plugins: { oidcProvider: false }`. Their manager stand-ins carry only the catch-all and bridge seams. Before this change, the discovery mount failed asynchronously on every one of their runs and the error went into a logger mock. With the mount synchronous, they read `getAuthIssuer` from a stub that did not have it.

## Production-shaped boot measurement (the triage raise rule)

`objectstack start` (NODE_ENV=production, empty kernel, default composition, local SQLite, fresh home) was booted through the real CLI dist in this container. The readiness probe was `GET /api/v1/health`, fired every 5 ms until the socket answered. Both doors were read 3 s later. The idle control waits 5 s after the socket opens before the first HTTP request. Times are ms since spawn, on a shared box.

| Leg | async-or-sync mount line | HTTP server started | first request | doors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pre-fix dist, early 1 | 6292 | 6523 | 6545 (200) | 200 / 200 |
| pre-fix dist, early 2 | 5806 | 6098 | 6120 (200) | 200 / 200 |
| pre-fix dist, early 3 | 6079 | 6293 | 6312 (200) | 200 / 200 |
| pre-fix dist, idle control | 5516 | 5713 | 10719 | 200 / 200 |
| fixed dist, early | 5444 | 6064 | 6091 (200) | 200 / 200 |
| fixed dist, idle control | 6173 | 6930 | 11937 | 200 / 200 |

On this boot shape, the pre-fix async mount landed 197 to 292 ms **before** the socket opened in 3 of 3 runs, so the window was not hit. **The raise rule is not met by this measurement.** NOT MEASURED: the cloud control-plane composition where the card measured the 404, and any boot against a remote database, where the instance build is longer. The pre-fix dist was planted and verified with `ablation-dist-preflight` (marker present), then restored and rebuilt, and the preflight confirmed the marker absent. No boot in either leg logged an ERROR line.

## Local verification (HEAD `eb85e827`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 116 files, 2480 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth run typecheck`: exit 0. `check:test-typecheck` held at 10 files, 94 errors, 23 signatures. The new test file compiles clean.
- Dependency closure: `turbo run build --filter='@objectstack/cli...'`, 59 tasks, exit 0.
- Lint, narrowed and proven: eslint `--no-inline-config --format json` over the 5 touched TS files reported 5 files linted, 0 errors and 0 warnings. The population is every `**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}` (`eslint.config.mjs`). This repo never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file.
- Derived gates (`dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, 65 commands): all 65 run at `eb85e827` with exit codes recorded, and all 65 exit 0. `--ran` reconciliation: 65 derived, 65 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3) because nine unrelated packages had no `dist/`. Once their `dist/` was present it was re-run and exited 0 (105 entry points across 66 packages load). `check:auth-mount-ledger`: OK, 20 auth mounts all accounted for. `check:nul-bytes`: OK.

## Acceptance notes

- `scripts/publish-smoke.sh` says plugin-auth logs the anchor line "when OIDC discovery route registration throws". After this change, a route that cannot be registered fails the boot instead, and the anchor line means the discovery documents could not be prepared from the auth instance. The pattern still matches and its gate still works. Only the comment is stale. Carrier: none.
- `auth-manager.ts` (the `authBuild` docblock) and the `auth-manager-instance-single-flight.test.ts` header still name "`registerOidcDiscoveryRoutes()` with `void`" as the boot caller of `getAuthInstance()`. That caller is now the boot-time preparation call. The single-flight reasoning still holds. Those files are outside this card's file surface. Carrier: none.
- In the degraded-oauthProvider case, the plain-HTTP transport notices are now emitted at mount, before the instance exists. On a public plain-HTTP origin, that notice says the documents are reachable. The degraded ERROR line that follows says they are not served, and it decides what clients get.

#21078 is the only card this PR closes.
